title: Dimension of symmetric trace-zero matrices
stem: Let $W$ be the vector space of real symmetric $4\times4$ matrices whose trace is zero. What is $\dim W$?
solution: A symmetric four-by-four matrix is determined by four diagonal entries and six entries strictly above the diagonal. Thus the full symmetric space has dimension ten. Trace is a nonzero linear functional on this space: for example, its value on $E_{11}$ is one. Its kernel therefore has dimension $10-1=9$, giving option 2. To see the independence directly, use the six matrices $E_{ij}+E_{ji}$ for $i<j$ and the three matrices $E_{11}-E_{44},E_{22}-E_{44},E_{33}-E_{44}$. Their distinct off-diagonal and first three diagonal coordinates prove independence, and the trace condition forces the remaining diagonal coordinate. Option 1 omits the independent trace constraint. Options 3 and 4 incorrectly subtract further constraints; symmetry has already been included in the count of ten.

title: An orthonormal basis defines a projection, not a norm expansion
stem: Let $\{u_1,\ldots,u_n\}$ be an orthonormal basis of a subspace $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, with $n\le m$. Define $Px=\sum_{k=1}^n\langle x,u_k\rangle u_k$. Which statement is false?
options: $P$ is a linear operator from $\mathbb R^m$ to $U$.
solution: Every image is a linear combination of the basis vectors, so it lies in $U$. Linearity follows from linearity of the real inner product in $x$. If $x=\sum a_ku_k$ belongs to $U$, orthonormality gives $\langle x,u_k\rangle=a_k$, hence $Px=x$; in particular, $P(Px)=Px$. Moreover $r=x-Px$ is orthogonal to every $u_k$ because $\langle r,u_j\rangle=\langle x,u_j\rangle-\langle x,u_j\rangle=0$. The orthogonal decomposition gives $\|x\|_2^2=\|Px\|_2^2+\|r\|_2^2$, so the universally valid inequality is $\|Px\|_2\le\|x\|_2$. The inequality in option 3 is not valid for arbitrary permitted subspaces: take $U=\operatorname{span}\{(1,0)\}$ and $x=(0,1)$. Then $Px=0$ while $\|x\|_2=1$. If $U=\mathbb R^m$, both norms agree; that special case does not establish option 3 as a general statement. The animation uses a two-dimensional orthogonal decomposition with labelled actual lengths, rather than pretending to draw arbitrary $m$ dimensions.
